pa_bruner_run.blurb: Bruner Run is the farthest-downstream cliff of the climbing walls along the Lower Yough gorge in Ohiopyle State Park, set beside the river's Bruner Run landing and the bike trail. A dozen climbs on sandstone mix sport leads, top ropes and a few trad lines, mostly short to mid-height. Difficulty skews hard: half a dozen sit in the 5.10 range and a few in the 5.11s, with just a couple of easy 5.6 to 5.7 climbs and a single 5.13 at the top end. A short woods walk on a blazed trail leads in, which makes it a handy stop for a few quality face climbs.

pa_3_75_cat_fish_cliff_area.blurb: This small sport crag is one stop along the Safe Harbor North cliffs, on the Enola Low Grade rail trail near Safe Harbor. The routes sit beside the trail close to a waterfall, with benches and a table nearby, so it is easy to reach on foot or by bike. Of the 11 climbs, ten are bolted sport leads and one is a top rope. Grades run from the high 5.7s up to 5.12, with a cluster of 5.8 to 5.10 lines that suit climbers working through the middle grades, and a pair of harder 5.12 routes for projecting.

pa_cave_the.blurb: The Cave is a bouldering sector in the Governor Stable boulder field of south-central Pennsylvania. Its centerpiece is an enormous diabase block perched on smaller stones, leaving a roofed chamber below that is not a true cave. The area holds 11 problems, many of them tall. The spread is wide: a handful of easy lines from VB to V2, a middle group around V4 to V7, and a couple of serious hard problems that reach V10 and V12. A few classics sit on the faces around the chamber, so bring plenty of pads for the high landings.

pa_warm_up_boulder.blurb: Warm up boulder is a pair of low-angle blocks on the hillside at Hay Creek Boulders in Berks County, among the first rocks you meet when coming up the Dye Cut mountain bike trail from the east. The 11 problems are friendly: nearly all are VB or V0 with one V1 and a single V3, and some easy scrambling is mixed in. The slabby rock on the left side is the better of the two. It works well as an opener before heading higher up the slope, or as a mellow spot for newer boulderers.

pa_painted_rocks.blurb: Painted Rocks is a small cluster of boulders in the Bauer Rock zone of South Mountain, reached by a short walk from the grassy clearing at the start of the trail, where a big jumble of rocks greets you on the right. It holds 11 problems, and the grades are gentle: the bulk fall between VB and V1, with a pair around V3 and one hard V5 at the top. With grades this low, it suits beginners and anyone after an easy circuit.
